note: Container-operation walkthrough by an agent, not a human operator study. Commands ran against disposable Compose projects owned by this walkthrough. Secrets, cookies, mail bodies and links are not recorded; command output is reduced to exit codes and selected sanitized lines.

images.note: During the run a parallel lab built the same revision and moved the tags openlaw-local:57e77e38... and openlaw-engine-local:57e77e38... to its own image IDs. Later up commands in this run then used those IDs. The reviewer compared both pairs: RootFS layers, Cmd, Entrypoint and Env are identical, and the images differ only in their Compose build labels (project name).

steps.action: docker compose restart does not apply a changed .env
steps.expected: After setting MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 and restarting, the app still has the old environment.
steps.actual: After adding MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 and docker compose restart app, the container's MAX_UPLOAD_MB was still empty and a 1,100,000-byte upload was accepted (201).

steps.action: up -d --no-build --pull never applies it; MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 refuses a larger upload and accepts a smaller one
steps.expected: The recreated app enforces the 1 MB ceiling.
steps.actual: up -d --no-build --pull never recreated the app; MAX_UPLOAD_MB is now 1 in the container. The 1,100,000-byte upload was refused with 413 "That file is over the 1 MB upload limit."; a 200,000-byte upload was accepted (201). The Caddy proxy has no body limit configured, so the app's own refusal was seen.

steps.action: An unreadable MAX_UPLOAD_MB falls back to the default instead of stopping startup
steps.expected: MAX_UPLOAD_MB=ten starts normally and accepts a 1.1 MB upload.
steps.actual: With MAX_UPLOAD_MB=ten the app started (/readyz 200) and accepted the 1,100,000-byte upload (201), so the ceiling fell back to the 100 MB default. The setting was then removed and the containers recreated.

steps.action: Return new writes to local while keeping s3 and azure-blob readers configured
steps.expected: All three stores stay readable.
steps.actual: Removed STORAGE_DRIVER (default local) and kept the S3 and Azure reader settings. A new local upload returned 201. Downloads: local 200 match, s3 200 match, azure 200 match, localAgain 200 match.

steps.action: DOC_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_MS above 420000 stops app and worker startup

installTiming.basis: Timestamps written by walkthrough-r2-1.mjs. docker compose build finished in 2 s because the layer cache already held this revision from parallel labs. First-run setup and the working-installation checks needed one database reset and retries (see failureNotes), so no end-to-end interval is claimed for them. This is one fast host, not a claim about a cold host or about DNS, TLS and proxy provisioning time.

fixtureImages.privateProxy: caddy:2-alpine with a certificate from a fictional CA created by the reviewer

failureNotes.note: Create Administrator: the POST reached the app and created the user and a session, but the browser got no answer and showed "The server could not be reached. Try again." The app logged no completion and the proxy logged no error. The next three steps failed because the wizard never opened. A curl probe through the same proxy answered 201 in 0.09 s. The reviewer reset the database (firstrun-reset) and the repeated steps passed. A later browser probe on this host saw Chromium abort a request with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED while parallel labs changed host networks. That fits the symptom, but it was not captured for this request.
Invitation link: the password was stored (sign-in with it answered 200 later), but the page did not show Password set within 30 s. Same symptom as above.
The retry reopened the already used link and correctly got "This link has expired or was already used. Ask for a new one."
Settings -> Users did not show Invite user within 30 s. A browser probe right after loaded the page with Invite user present. The repeated step passed.

The selectors expected Email me a sign-in link and Set up or reset your password on the sign-in page. This build hides both while email is not configured. Replaced by mail-no-from-requests and mail-no-from-password-setup.

Article (Configure outbound email and providers): with SMTP_URL set and no From address, "the test email, sign-in link requests, and password-setup requests report that email is unavailable". Observed: the test email answers 502 "SMTP is not configured - save a relay first" and a sign-in link request answers 403 "Sign-in links are unavailable: this instance cannot send email. Contact your administrator." A password-setup request answers 503 with title "Internal server error" and no detail. The route raises "Email is not configured. Contact your administrator.", but the app does not expose 5xx messages, so that text is only in the app log. The sign-in page offers neither Set up or reset your password nor Email me a sign-in link in this state, so a person cannot start either request there. No email reached the relay. Before the scripted check, a reviewer curl probe outside the script sent the same request for Rowan Operator with the same environment and saw the same 503 answer and log line; the environment was then restored.
A sign-in check used the direct address as Origin and got 403. The check was removed and the step passed in private-apply.

A container on the default bridge network could not reach either the direct port or the working proxy on 172.17.0.1, so it could not stand in for another device. The cause was not investigated. Replaced by checks from the host's other addresses in private-serve.

Node-side API requests could not resolve the placeholder hostname; the browser used --host-resolver-rules. The script then mapped the hostname in Node as well. The later password-setup attempt for Rowan Operator got 429 from the per-address request limit after this run's earlier requests, and the check then used Avery Morgan. The earlier-email check first read the newest message instead of the first invitation.

install.basis: Every V-C44 step passed on its final attempt. Failed entries stay in the log: two lost browser answers (environment), one environment timeout on Settings -> Users, and one reviewer checker fault, each followed by a recorded reset or retry.

deployment-configuration.failure: With SMTP_URL set and SMTP_FROM unset, a password-setup request does not report that email is unavailable. POST /api/v1/auth/password-setup answers 503 "Internal server error" with no detail, and the sign-in page hides Set up or reset your password. The article says password-setup requests report that email is unavailable.
deployment-configuration.otherChecks: All other V-C45 checks passed on their final attempt: restart versus up, upload ceiling and fallback, topology, engine defaults, proxy origin and wrong origin, upload/download and live update through the proxy, local/s3/azure-blob storage with retained readers, storage validation and an unreachable reader, engine bounds and an unavailable engine, external database and its negatives, the saved wizard relay, the environment SMTP pin and its removal, test email and sign-in link refusals without SMTP_FROM, the invitation without SMTP_FROM (#889 behavior as the article describes), the wizard that cannot finish, no email Settings page, key rotation, wrong/missing/short key, AUTH_SECRET session invalidation, and the Deploy on a private VM path (!override, loopback-only app port, supplied-certificate Caddy site with bind and headers, BASE_URL recreation, links on the private hostname, old emails unchanged, upload/download/processing and live update through the private proxy).

teardown: Both owned projects were removed with docker compose -p <project> down -v --remove-orphans, including the private proxy service. No containers, volumes or networks with either project label remain. The shared image tags stay in the local cache. The private clone, .env, fixture passwords, certificates and browser screenshots were deleted after the run.
limitations: Independent agent container-operation walkthrough, not a human operator study.
HTTPS for the install check used Caddy's internal CA for openlaw-r2.localhost, accepted only in the reviewer's browser context.

The private VM check used a fictional CA, the placeholder hostname openlaw-r2.company.example:23327 bound to the host bridge address 172.17.0.1 and resolved by browser and Node mappings, not internal DNS. Host port 3000 was already in use, so the mapping and proxy upstream were changed together to 23320 as the article allows. VPN routing, firewall and IPv6 rules, corporate CA trust on employee devices, DNS-01 issuance and access from a real second device were not tested.

No OIDC provider was configured; GET /api/auth/sso/callback answered 302 from the API on the private origin, but an SSO return was not tested. Signing Polling and Webhook modes were not part of this run.
The SMTP relay was an owned Mailpit container without authentication.
Known issue #889 (invitations report success when SMTP_FROM is unset) is open; the run confirmed the behavior the article describes.
